text_blocks.snippet: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recently updated their Respiratory Virus Guidance, recommending that individuals stay home and away from others until at least 24 hours after their symptoms are improving overall and they have no fever (without using fever-reducing medication). This updated guidance applies to various respiratory illnesses, including COVID-19, and may result in shorter, same, or longer isolation periods compared to previous guidelines, depending on the individual's symptoms. Additionally, COVID-19 vaccine recommendations have been updated, with the CDC recommending a 2024-2025 COVID-19 vaccine for most adults 18 and older.

list.title: Updated Respiratory Virus Guidance:
list.snippet: The CDC's updated guidance on respiratory viruses, including COVID-19, emphasizes staying home and away from others until both symptom improvement and fever resolution (without medication) are achieved, according to the CDC. This replaces previous specific isolation timelines for COVID-19 with a more flexible approach based on individual symptom progression.

list.title: 2024-2025 COVID-19 Vaccine:
list.snippet: The CDC recommends that most adults ages 18 and older receive the 2024-2025 COVID-19 vaccine. Information about updated vaccine recommendations for other age groups, including children, can be found on the CDC's website.
